peerMapping.justification: Three-run Kimi K3 consensus selected only the displayed peers: MU 30.0% with 3/3 replicate support; SKHX 26.7% with 3/3 replicate support; SMSN 20.0% with 3/3 replicate support; SNDK 15.0% with 3/3 replicate support; DRAM 8.3% with 2/3 replicate support. Individual rationales state each economic relationship.

peers.name: Micron Technology
peers.reason: Micron is the closest pure-play economic comparator: a memory manufacturer whose revenue is overwhelmingly DRAM and NAND, exposed to the same spot and contract pricing cycle, the same capital expenditure and wafer supply dynamics, and the same data center and AI memory demand drivers as CXMT. It carries deep 24-hour perp liquidity of 59.489 USD millions, making it both the most similar and a readily executable peer.

peers.name: SK hynix common
peers.reason: SK hynix common is a direct DRAM and HBM competitor selling into the same memory cycle and sharing the same customers and capex and wafer cost structure, making it a same-underlying-exposure peer. I use the common line rather than the SK hynix ADR because the directly traded underlying is preferred over the ADR wrapper, and the common line also has higher 24-hour liquidity at about 104.714 versus 32.365 USD millions, which is only an execution tie-breaker on top of the economic match.

peers.name: Samsung Electronics common
peers.reason: Samsung Electronics common is the largest merchant DRAM producer and therefore a direct substitute for CXMT's core exposure, with shared memory pricing and input costs. It is weighted slightly below the two pure plays because its returns are also driven by foundry, logic, smartphones, and consumer devices, which dilute the clean DRAM signal even though the memory franchise is dominant.

peers.name: Sandisk
peers.reason: Sandisk is a pure memory name that shares the broader memory-storage cycle and fab input-cost exposure with CXMT, so it is a legitimate economic peer rather than a factor analogy. It receives the lowest weight because it is NAND-flash centric while CXMT is DRAM centric, so its end-market pricing driver is related but not identical; its very high 24-hour liquidity of about 250.017 USD millions is treated as execution convenience, not as evidence of closer similarity.

peers.name: Roundhill Memory ETF
peers.reason: The Roundhill Memory ETF also belongs in the peer basket because it is a traded basket of exactly the global memory producers that define CXMT's pricing environment. It captures the sector-wide return exposure that no single name can, and the guidance allows a broad or sector index to carry a large peer weight when it captures a major share of the target's return exposure; here it is held at a moderate weight alongside the single-name direct competitors.

primary_index_hedge.name: Roundhill Memory ETF
primary_index_hedge.reason: CXMT is a merchant DRAM maker, so its dominant systematic driver is the global memory pricing cycle rather than generic equity beta. The Roundhill Memory ETF is the eligible equity_etf that most directly tracks that memory-cycle factor, so hedging with it isolates CXMT's idiosyncratic and China-specific component instead of merely removing broad market risk. Its 24-hour liquidity of about 63.645 USD millions is adequate for execution and is in line with Micron, so the hedge is tradable. I prefer it over the leveraged SOXL wrapper and over broad SP500 or XYZ100, which would only capture generic risk-on co-movement.

peerMapping.historyMethod: daily-rebalanced peer spot total returns using the fixed Kimi weights; the basket begins with the first available selected peer, unavailable pre-listing peers are omitted, and remaining weights are renormalized; the browser rebases the basket to the target spot level at the first shared date of each selected chart range

liveSplice.method: current Hyperliquid native or TradeXYZ perp mid divided by that peer's matching-venue perp close on its latest spot date; available Kimi weights are renormalized and applied as a one-period return from the published peer spot endpoint; USD cash close is retained for disclosure but never mixed with a differently scaled perp contract
